source_text: ubi coheredem invenit unicum per naturam, adoptatus ipse per gratiam eique tantum concupiscentiam carnalem mortem non inferre post mortem, qui in Christi morte invenerit mortem, qua moriatur peccato, et evaserit mortem qua natus fuerat in peccato. Ad omnia me tibi respondisse, Iuliane, et omnia refellisse, quibus putasti et disputasti voluminibus quattuor credendum non esse originale peccatum, et concupiscentiam carnis non posse culpari sine damnatione nuptiarum
pass_a_gloss: Where coheredem invenit unicum through nature, adoptatus himself through grace eique only desire carnalem death not inferre after death, who in of-Christ by-death invenerit death, where moriatur by-sin, and evaserit death where born fuerat in by-sin. to all-things me to-you respondisse, Iuliane, and all-things refellisse, to-whom putasti and disputasti volumes four credendum not to-be original sin, and desire of-flesh not to-be-able culpari without damnatione of-marriages.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: Augustine reports Julian’s two main claims in his four books: original sin should not be believed, and sexual desire cannot be blamed without condemning marriage.

He also reports Julian’s claim that he has undertaken war against the ungodly and stands with the patriarchs, prophets, apostles, martyrs, and priests. Julian alleges that a company of Manicheans is defeating him.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
